newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. rates, local economy subdue Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rates, local economy subdue Singapore shares.

text.p: Singapore shares opened flat on Wednesday with buyers subdued after a 0.25 percentage point rise in U.S. interest rates and no positive domestic news to breathe life back into the market, dealers said.
"The U.S. news has been factored in, but there's still some downside potential locally," a dealer with a local firm said.
"There's no real incentive to get this market going. Our economy is down, electronics are down, shipping is down. The best we can hope for is a holding pattern," another dealer said.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 1.19 at 2,101.14 at 0235 GMT on thin volume of 32.8 million shares.
Most interest in early trade was from retail buyers with institutional investors and large foreign funds firmly sidelined, dealers said.
Retail buying fuelled a rise in Vickers Ballas, dealers said, up Singapore $0.27 to S$2.51 on news of a 41 percent leap in profits and a one-for-one bonus issue.
North Borneo Timber led 156 early gainers, up S$0.40 at S$11.10 on thin volume.
Creative Technology stock topped 55 early losers, down S$0.40 at S$14.40.
